'''Uta Paszkowski''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|FRS}} (born 1964) is a German biologist specializing in molecular genetics of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis in cereals. Since 2026 she has been Russell R. Geiger Professor of Crop Science and director of the [[Crop Science Centre]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].

== Early life and education ==
Paszkowski undertook undergraduate study at the [[University of Cologne]].<ref name="NAS bio" /> She earned a ''[[Diplom]]'' ([[master's degree]]) in [[phytopathology]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research]].<ref name="CSC bio">{{cite web |title=Uta Paszkowski, Director of the Crop Science Centre |url=https://www.cropsciencecentre.org/staff/uta-paszkowski/ |website=Crop Science Centre |access-date=7 August 2026}}</ref> She completed her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree in [[biotechnology]] at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="FRS bio">{{cite web |title=Professor Uta Paszkowski FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/uta-paszkowski-38130/ |website=royalsociety.org |publisher=The Royal Society |access-date=7 August 2026 |language=en |date=2026}}</ref><ref name="ENSA bio">{{cite web |title=Uta Paszkowski |url=https://www.ensa.ac.uk/team/uta-paszkowski/ |website=ENSA |access-date=7 August 2026}}</ref> Her research focused on [[gene targeting]] in tobacco.<ref name="ENSA bio" />

== Academic career and research ==
Following postdoctoral work on AM symbiosis at the [[University of Basel]] and the Syngenta Torrey Mesa Research Institute, she held academic positions at the [[University of Geneva]] and the [[University of Lausanne]].<ref name="FRS bio"/><ref name="PlantSci-Chair">{{cite web |title=Uta Paszkowski appointed Director of the Crop Science Centre |url=https://www.plantsci.cam.ac.uk/news/uta-paszkowski-appointed-director-crop-science-centre-and-russell-r-geiger-professor-crop |website=plantsci.cam.ac.uk |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref>

She joined the [[University of Cambridge]] in October 2012 as a [[lecturer]].<ref name="ENSA bio" /> She was promoted to [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in 2017.<ref name="ENSA bio" /> She was made Professor of Plant Molecular Genetics in 2019.<ref>{{cite web  |title=Senior Academic Promotions, 1 October 2019 exercise: Appointments and titles  |url=https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2018-19/weekly/6557/section3.shtml  |website=Cambridge University Reporter  |publisher=University of Cambridge  |date=24 July 2019  |access-date=7 August 2026 }}</ref> She is a [[Fellow (Oxbridge)|fellow]] of [[St John's College, Cambridge]],<ref name="St J FRS">{{cite web |title=Leading plant scientist elected to prestigious Royal Society Fellowship |url=https://www.joh.cam.ac.uk/about-us/news-and-research/leading-plant-scientist-elected-to-prestigious-royal-society-fellowship |website=St John's College |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=7 August 2026 |date=27 May 2026}}</ref> where she is director of studies for plant sciences.<ref name="St J Bio">{{cite web |title=Professor Uta Paszkowski |url=https://www.joh.cam.ac.uk/research/academics/fellows/professor-uta-paszkowski |website=St John's College |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=7 August 2026}}</ref> In 2026, she was additionally appointed Russell R. Geiger Chair in Crop Science in the [[Department of Plant Sciences, University of Cambridge]], and director of the [[Crop Science Centre]].<ref name="appointed CSC Director">{{cite web |title=Uta Paszkowski appointed CSC Director and Russell R. Geiger Professor of Crop Science |url=https://www.plantsci.cam.ac.uk/news/uta-paszkowski-appointed-csc-director-and-russell-r-geiger-professor-crop-science |website=Department of Plant Sciences |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=7 August 2026 |language=en |date=1 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="CSC Bio">{{cite web |title=Uta Paszkowski, Director of the Crop Science Centre |url=https://www.cropsciencecentre.org/staff/uta-paszkowski/ |website=cropsciencecentre.org |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref>

Her research focuses on improving [[agricultural sustainability]] by studying how cereals take up nutrients via symbiotic fungi.<ref name="PlantSci-Chair"/>

==Honours==
In 2020, was elected as a member to the [[European Molecular Biology Organisation]].<ref name="EMBO">{{cite web |title=EMBO Member: Uta Paszkowski |url=https://people.embo.org/profile/uta-paszkowski |website=people.embo.org |publisher=European Molecular Biology Organisation |access-date=7 August 2026}}</ref>

She was elected to the Leopoldina (2023). In 2025, she was elected an [[Member of the National Academy of Sciences|international member]] of the American [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="NAS bio">{{cite web |title=Uta Paszkowski |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/uta-paszkowski-1fjqtr/ |website= nasonline.org |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=7 August 2026 |date=2025}}</ref> In 2026, she was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS), United Kingdom's national academy of sciences.<ref name="Cam RS">{{cite web |title=Cambridge researchers elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://www.cam.ac.uk/research/news/cambridge-researchers-elected-as-fellows-of-the-royal-society-2026 |website=cam.ac.uk |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref>
